title: Wildfire Smoke and Bad Air
summary: Check the air quality. Stay in with clean air. Use a well-fitting N95 if you must go out.
steps: Check the Air Quality Index (AirNow or local alerts). Orange (101+) or worse: sensitive people stay indoors. Red (151+): everyone cut back outdoors.
Keep windows and doors closed. Run air conditioning on recirculate with a clean filter. No fans that pull in outside air.
Make a clean-air room: one room, door closed, a HEPA air cleaner running.
Going out: wear a tight-fitting N95 respirator. Cloth and surgical masks do not stop smoke particles.
Skip hard exercise. Avoid candles, gas stoves, frying and vacuuming without a HEPA filter.
Trouble breathing, chest pain or dizziness: follow your asthma plan and call 911 if severe.
dont: Do not open windows to air out the house while smoke lasts.
warn: Children, older adults, pregnant people and anyone with heart or lung disease are at higher risk.

title: Boat Emergency
summary: Life jackets on. Stay with a capsized boat. Call for help on VHF 16 or 911. Reach or throw, do not jump in.
steps: Everyone puts on a life jacket now.
Call for help: VHF channel 16, say Mayday three times, then boat name, position, problem and number aboard. Or call 911 on a phone.
Capsized: stay with the boat and climb onto it if you can. It floats and is easier to see.
Person overboard: shout, point and keep eyes on them, throw anything that floats, slow down and turn back. Reach or throw. Do not jump in.
Cold water: control your breathing first. Keep your life jacket on and curl up to save heat.
Fuel smell or fire: stop the engine and fuel, move people upwind, use an extinguisher. Keep away from engine exhaust.
dont: Do not try to swim for shore unless it is very close.
Do not go back in for gear.
warn: Carbon monoxide builds up near engines and generators on boats.

title: Electric Shock or Lightning Strike
summary: Do not touch until the power is off. Call 911. Lightning victims carry no charge: start CPR.
steps: Do not touch the person until the power is off. Switch it off, or push the source away with something dry like wood. Downed lines: stay 35 feet back.
Call 911.
Not breathing normally: start CPR and use an AED.
Lightning strike: the person carries no charge, so it is safe to touch. If several people were struck, help the ones who look lifeless first.
Cool burns with running water and cover loosely.
Keep them warm and lying down. Everyone shocked or struck needs medical evaluation, even if they feel fine.
dont: Do not touch someone who may still be in contact with a live wire.
Do not use anything wet or metal to move a wire.
warn: Electric shock can cause a delayed, dangerous heart rhythm.

title: Emergency Abroad: Which Number?
summary: Emergency numbers differ by country. Look yours up before you travel. Try 112 if unsure.
steps: 112 is the emergency number across the EU and in many other countries. 911: U.S., Canada, Mexico. 999: UK. 000: Australia. 111: New Zealand. 110 police and 119 fire or ambulance: Japan.
Say where you are first, in simple words. Ask for an English speaker.
Contact your insurer's assistance line early for medical emergencies.
Lost passport, arrest or serious injury: contact your embassy or consulate.
Disaster or unrest: follow local authorities, move to a safe place and message family.
dont: Do not assume the number is 911.
Do not rely on one phone or one card. Carry paper copies.
warn: Numbers change. Confirm them before you travel and save them on paper and in your phone.
